label: first token is d (strong) or b (weak)
explanation: Fires only at step 0 (the first original token), and only when that token is d or b. When it is d the activation is near-constant at max (~1.335, 95% of mass). When it is b it is about 0.05 of max (~0.067). The predicate is exact on dev (P=R=1). It never fires at any later step, on any other first token, or in the delimiter or copy phases. L and the rest of the sequence do not modulate it. The dev correlation is 0.999 with the d-only predicate, so magnitude is basically a d indicator plus a small b component.

issues: No refutation found. Test split: predicate (t==0)&isin(in_tok,[d,b]) has P=1.0, R=1.0, F1=1.0, mass recall 1.0. Test misses: 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

Profile confirms the factual claims. All activity is at t=0 (100% of mass) and none in the delimiter or copy phases. Only in_tok d (0.953 of mass) and b (0.047) fire; the firing rate is identical for d and b (~0.084). The median activation (1.335) equals the max, so d is near-constant at max. The b examples show about 0.05 of max (max 0.067).

The d-only predicate on test gives F1 0.669, mass recall 0.953 and correlation 0.9988, consistent with the explanation. The full predicate's correlation is 0.742 because it treats b as equal to d. That is fine, since the label says b is weak.

The by-L variation (rate 0.011 to 0.004) is just the share of t=0 steps in shorter sequences. Per-sequence counts are flat at about 5.4k for each L>=4, so sequence length does not modulate the feature.
Minor nit: the profile reports a 0.999 correlation for d-only, which matches test (0.9988).
